subject: pathology
title: Haemangiomas, Pyogenic Granuloma, Glomus Tumour, Kaposi Sarcoma, and Angiosarcoma

steps.tx: Vascular tumours span infantile haemangiomas that proliferate then involute, malformations that grow with the child, and malignant angiosarcomas, separated by GLUT1 staining and clinical tempo. The common infant tumour is the **infantile haemangioma (GLUT1 positive)**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Infantile haemangiomas proliferate, plateau, and involute; GLUT1 separates them from malformations.

steps.tx: Propranolol revolutionised complicated infantile haemangiomas threatening vision, airway, or ulcerating skin, shrinking lesions through vasoconstriction and antiangiogenic effects after cardiovascular screening. That first line drug therapy is **propranolol for infantile haemangioma**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Propranolol after screening shrinks threatening infantile haemangiomas; timolol serves small superficial ones.

rows: Bruise like scalp or breast lesion, elderly

steps.tx: Pyogenic granuloma is neither pyogenic nor granuloma but a lobular capillary proliferation erupting after trauma or pregnancy hormones, bleeding profusely from a friable red stalk and recurring if incompletely excised. The misnamed bleeder is **pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary haemangioma)**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: A friable red nodule bleeding after trivial trauma is pyogenic granuloma; excise it and send histology.

steps.tx: Glomus tumours arise from thermoregulatory glomus bodies, classically subungual, with pinpoint pain, cold sensitivity, and tenderness localised by a pinhead, cured by complete excision. The painful nail tumour is the **glomus tumour of the nail unit**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Pinpoint subungual pain with cold agony means glomus tumour; excision cures what imaging hunts.

vis.caption: Subungual glomus tumour beneath the nail with classic painful presentation.

steps.tx: Kaposi sarcoma, driven by human herpesvirus 8 in immunosuppression, paints violaceous patches, plaques, and nodules on skin, mouth, gut, and lung, regressing substantially when HIV therapy restores immunity. The HHV8 tumour is **Kaposi sarcoma in immunosuppression**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Violaceous plaques plus immunosuppression mean Kaposi sarcoma; restoring immunity is its first chemotherapy.

vis.caption: Kaposi sarcoma violaceous plaques in advanced immunosuppression.

steps.tx: Angiosarcoma bruises elderly scalps, irradiated breasts, and chronically lymphoedematous arms with malignant endothelium that metastasises early and answers poorly, demanding wide oncology margins and trials. Stewart-Treves names its lymphoedema form: **angiosarcoma including Stewart-Treves syndrome**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: A spreading bruise on an elderly scalp or irradiated breast is angiosarcoma until biopsy acquits it.

steps.tx: Epithelioid haemangioendothelioma and Kaposi sarcoma remind us vascular malignancy grades between haemangioma innocence and angiosarcoma fury, with HHV8 staining and MYC amplification sorting radiation associated cases. Panel discipline is **vascular tumour immunohistochemistry triage**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: HHV8, ERG, CD31, and MYC sort vascular tumours better than appearance alone ever will.

steps.tx: Bleeding vascular lesions punish blind cautery without histology, because pyogenic granuloma mimics amelanotic melanoma and angiosarcoma mimics bruising, so excised tissue always reaches pathology. That rule is **histology for every excised vascular lesion**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Every excised red nodule earns histology; melanoma and angiosarcoma both masquerade as benign bleeders.
